newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Unwelcome silence ends for Singapore mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Unwelcome silence ends for Singapore mobile phones.

text.p: It was ringing and beeping as usual on Sunday for Singapore's legions of mobile phone and pager users, after a breakdown in the system was resolved late on Saturday.

The Straits Times daily newspaper quoted Singapore Telecommunications (SingTel) as saying problems affecting the island's mobile and pager networks, which began early in the afternoon and persisted well into the evening, were resolved by 9.30 p.m. (1330 GMT).

A mobile phone in the hand or a pager on the belt is almost as common as a watch on the wrist in this affluent city state, with some 1.2 million pager or mobile phone subscribers. Singapore's total population is about three million.
SingTel attributed the problem to congestion caused by a software fault in a switch that connects the fixed telephone, mobile and paging networks, the Straits Times said.
SingTel spokesmen could not be reached immediately for comment on Sunday.
The Telecommunications Authority of Singapore has asked SingTel to investigate and report on the disruption.
